blindSummary:
This is an extreme-risk destination for trans visitors. The penal code criminalises "illicit sexual intercourse" and "indecent acts" (up to 5 years), and a rights-research group documents de-facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity and transition through these provisions — compounded by recent religious rulings declaring the very term "gender" religiously forbidden, making anyone using it in media or institutions susceptible to prosecution. Militias control territory and operate detention sites where torture is systematic; there is no functioning central judiciary, no legal gender recognition, and no protection of any kind.

For a visitor: detention by any of several militia authorities is the modal bad outcome, with no consular reach in much of the country.
blindOutOfScope: Militia fragmentation means enforcement varies by territory; the trans-specific mechanism is documented de-facto criminalisation.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional rights-research group country review: de facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity and transition (social, medical, surgical) via 'indecent acts' and 'illicit intercourse' provisions; recent religious rulings designate the term 'gender' as religiously forbidden, exposing users to punishment; no legal gender recognition framework or court attempts; armed militias retaliate against gender-diverse people amid the post-2011 conflict.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity criminalised (up to 5 years under 'illicit sexual intercourse' and 'indecent acts' provisions applying to men and women); no SOGIESC protections; no legal gender recognition; enforcement and repression intensified after 2011 - armed groups and security agencies arrest people based on perceived orientation or gender identity, with discrimination, violence and arbitrary detention.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying international legal-aid trust country profile documents this country's criminalisation of same-sex activity.

Foreign broadsheet (June 2016): a widely shared explainer on the situation of gay people in states with religious-law systems - the official fiction is that gay people do not exist across this region; family and societal attitudes are often a bigger problem than state persecution; this country among those covered.

International human-rights organisation (June 2015): report on a territorial extremist organisation's war on gay men - documents public executions of men accused of homosexuality in territories it controlled, including in this country.

Development-sector news outlet (June 2015): the situation for gay people in this country is getting worse - the extremist organisation executed three young men in a coastal city (kneeling in plastic tubs, shot in the back of the head before a crowd); considered the first death sentences for homosexuality in this country's modern history; no one in that city dares speak of the killings.

News site (Nov 2012): report that 12 men accused of being gay faced torture and death by an armed militia - NOTE: the original source was a social-media page falsely claiming affiliation with an international human-rights organisation, which later apologised for misrepresenting itself; treat with caution.
blindTangential: “Illicit sexual intercourse” and “indecent acts” provisions (up to 5 years) capture same-sex conduct and gender nonconformity alike.
